A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same VSTAR paper and Appendices A–D. Text, equations, figures and embedded content match; only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp and PDF metadata differ.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original video-generation experiments and ablations. Appendix A includes DreamSim analyses and results from a 110-participant user study.

after.justification: The same original video-generation experiments, ablations, DreamSim analyses and 110-participant user study remain in Section 4 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: Video Synopsis Prompting, Temporal Attention Regularization and the optimization-based exploration in Appendix B are identical. No components, inference procedures or objectives change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same visual-transition prompts and real-video collection, including web and DAVIS examples described in Appendix D.2. No dataset, task, domain or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Figures 6–7 and S.7 retain ModelScope, LaVie, AnimateDiff and VideoCrafter2 as comparators. The user-study comparison against VideoCrafter2 and the ModelScope comparisons also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The VideoCrafter2 base model at 320 × 512 resolution, evaluated frame lengths, DreamSim procedures and 110-participant user-study design are identical in Section 4 and Appendix A.

E4.justification: The attention-resolution interventions, VSP/TAR component ablations, regularization-strength analysis and supplementary consistency and optimization analyses are all retained without revision.

E5.justification: Seed-related statements and statistical reporting are identical throughout the main text and appendices. No repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: All qualitative outputs, DreamSim plots and user-study results match. For example, Figure S.2 retains VSTAR temporal-coherency approval of 87.6% for 16-frame videos and 79.1% for 32–64-frame videos.

T1.justification: The attention and Gaussian-Toeplitz definitions in Section 3 and the covariance and optimization-loss formulations in Appendix B are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about training-free, single-pass dynamic video generation through VSP and TAR, and the contribution of temporal-attention analysis.

C2.justification: Interpretations of temporal attention, positional encoding and length generalization are unchanged. The prompt-alignment limitations, base-model constraints and optimization-cost tradeoffs are also identical.

D1.justification: Model settings, regularization parameters, Appendix C prompting instructions, the project-page link and the statement about prompt_list.json are unchanged. No reproducibility or access information is added.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 32 references are identical. Positioning relative to prior video-generation and attention-manipulation work, including novelty claims, remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1, dated 20 Mar 2024, to v2, dated 18 Mar 2025. The paper's prose, headings, terminology and section structure are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–12 and S.1–S.11 retain identical graphics, captions and placement. Page layouts are unchanged; the updated stamp text does not alter the layout.

improvement.justification: The later PDF preserves the same scientific content, empirical evidence, technical documentation and limitations, including all appendices. Updating only the arXiv stamp and PDF metadata produces no meaningful improvement or deterioration in paper quality.
